narrative_synthesis: The meta is still 'can a regular person get in' plus a fresh Philly local angle on zoning/short-term stays. Drafts: (1) Philly then-vs-now numbers Bar fills with real figures, (2) South Philly zoning ownership question, (3) creative-finance path when conventional math breaks.

drafts.draft_en:
Same Philly rowhome. Two different eras.

Then: bought for [$___], rent [$___]/mo, payment [$___]
Now: it'd cost [$___], rent [$___]/mo, payment [$___]

The deals didn't disappear. They moved to people who know how to structure them.
drafts.pattern: then-vs-now numbers (Jacob_Naviaux 6.8k, still the sticky format). Fill only with real figures from a deal you know; don't post with placeholders.
drafts.video_tip: Split-screen talking head, 25s: 'then' numbers on the left, 'now' on the right, appearing as you say them. End on the last line to camera.

drafts.draft_en:
South Philly just got a short-term stay project through with no zoning appeal.

State zoning talk is also heating up in Harrisburg.

If the rules for what gets built (and rented) keep shifting, who actually wins in Philly: the neighbor, the small investor, or the big operator?

Philly investors, what's your read?
drafts.pattern: local Philly signal (ninthhostage 10.4k South Philly STR + nextphlmayor 2.6k state zoning). Question post to own the local conversation.
drafts.video_tip: Selfie video on a South Philly block, 15s, point at a vacant or under-construction property, ask the question, end with 'tell me in the replies'.

drafts.draft_en:
People aren't mad about cement prices. They're mad that the old path into ownership feels closed.

When the bank math breaks, the next move isn't giving up. It's learning structures that still work: seller finance, subject-to, creative terms that fit both sides.

If conventional is locked, study the deals that still close. That's how you build a legacy when the easy door shuts.
drafts.pattern: cost-to-build / 'can regular people still get in' meta (degenBRO 76.4k climbing) plus creative-finance education. No health claims, no promised returns. Education, not advice.
drafts.video_tip: Walk-and-talk past a job site or rowhome, 20s. One line per cut. Put 'the old path feels closed' on screen, then cut to 'study the deals that still close'.
